page.layout: Running head "EMBLEMA" centred at top, page number 110 at top left. Title line across the full width. Below it, a full-width engraving (emblem picture) with inscriptions on a medallion and two pillars. Below the engraving, four lines of italic verse, the last line indented. At the right foot, the word "Homo".

main_text.l: Medallion: Lex frenum / Lex est speculum / Lex regula vitae
Left pillar: Diligē Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo.
Right pillar: Et proximum tuum sicut teipsum.

l.i: Est virtus geminis sublimibus alta columnis,
Illa Deum prendens, [illegible, ~6 letters] hæcce suum:
Inter namq; Deum currit dilectio, & inter
Proximum, vt hunc propter seruiat illi etiam.

page.notes: The engraving shows a hanging medallion with the inscription, two pillars with the commandments of love, a winged figure, and two stone tablets numbered 1 to 10. The Greek word in line 2 of the verse is not legible on the scan. Pillar and medallion inscriptions are reproduced in full-line form as printed, with the partly worn letters of the medallion transcribed as far as they can be read.
